From `src/presentations/&lt;slug&gt;/`, `../../presentation-kit` is `src/presentation-kit`, so these resolve. `steps/Scene.tsx` and `steps/index.ts` use `../../../presentation-kit/index.ts`, which resolves to the same place from `steps/`. `entities.ts` uses `../../presentation-kit/index.ts`. `talk.css` is among the template files, so the CSS import resolves, and `types: [&quot;vite/client&quot;]` in the bootstrap `tsconfig.app.json` covers the side-effect import. - **Kit exports.** The bootstrap `presentation-kit/index.ts` exports `Presentation`, `Appear`, `Box`, `SceneLayer`, `Rect`, `Step` and `SceneProps`, which are exactly the symbols the templates import. engineering-tests-wait-on-stateengineering-presentation-code-and-tests0 of 0.375 (minor)failthe span audit's stated contradiction was confirmed by an independent check: The requirement has two parts. Tests that drive a browser must wait for observable state through a polling or auto-waiting assertion, and they must use no fixed sleeps. The quoted material meets the first part but not the second. It does show state waits: inspect-presentation.mjs:65 waits with waitForFunction on data-step-index, and render.mjs:33-44 polls the index. But the browser tests also depend on fixed sleeps for transitions before they assert. The clearest case is the settling test (tests/integration/inspect.test.ts:139-151). It runs inspect with --settle=1200 and --settle=2500, which become page.waitForTimeout(args.settleMs) at inspect-presentation.mjs:67. It then asserts that the step-2 capture taken after the 1200 ms sleep equals the one taken after 2500 ms, and that the 0 ms capture differs. That assertion rests on a fixed wait for a transition to finish, not on a settled signal. The other inspect tests are similar: each passes --settle=300 (line 18), and the overlap, chrome and attribution warnings they assert on are computed after that fixed 300 ms sleep (lines 67-74). The e2e entrance-error tests (verify.test.ts:118-140) inject an error 900 ms after the step appears. They pass only because render.mjs:86 sleeps a fixed SETTLE_MS before check(i), with no state wait. The ruling argues that the settle runs after the index wait, and that &#39;longer fixed settle delays&#39; is validator noise. Neither point saves the pass. The noise clause only says no credit is given for, and nothing fails for the absence of, longer settle delays. It does not exempt existing fixed sleeps from the &#39;no fixed sleeps&#39; clause. The guidance also fails any test that &#39;waits a fixed number of milliseconds … for a transition before asserting&#39;. The pass claim says no fixed sleeps are used, and the material shows the opposite. | The requirement has two parts: browser tests must wait for observable state, and they must use no fixed sleeps. The inspect and verify templates land in `scripts/` next to a complete `scripts/lib/`. No focused test materializes and builds the created-presentation templates. `bootstrap.test.ts` builds only the bootstrap with its `starter` presentation. The verdict therefore rests on tracing alone. - **Relative imports.** `Talk.tsx` imports `../../presentation-kit/index.ts`, `./outline.ts`, `./steps/index.ts` and `./talk.css`. It does not answer the majority&#39;s reason for failing, which the material shows. The tests do start processes: run() in tests/helpers/project.ts spawns `npm run verify` and `node scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs`, which start the preview and browser. On timeout, run() calls child.kill(&#39;SIGKILL&#39;) only on its direct child, the npm wrapper. The shared Scene composes the kit&#39;s Appear, Arrow, Box, Frame, Label, SymbolChip, SceneLayer and the SceneProps type. Stage supplies `previous` only when the scene key is unchanged, and Scene reads it. steps/index.ts types the steps with the kit&#39;s Step and sets Scene, payload and groupKey, which Stage consumes. Nothing in the demo reimplements navigation, scaling, layout groups or chrome.","evidence":["Talk.tsx: `&lt;Presentation steps={STEPS} title={TITLE} initialMode=&quot;browse&quot; /&gt;`","Scene.tsx imports Appear, Arrow, Box, Frame, Label, SceneLayer, SymbolChip and SceneProps from the kit and uses `previous?.stage`.","steps/index.ts: `STEPS: Step&lt;ScenePayload&gt;[]` with Scene, payload and groupKey.","Stage.tsx passes `previous` into `&lt;Scene payload previous step&gt;` and uses `step.Scene`, `step.payload` and `sceneKey(step)`."],"citations":["src/presentations/how-to-make-a-presentation/Talk.tsx","src/presentations/how-to-make-a-presentation/steps/Scene.tsx","src/presentations/how-to-make-a-presentation/steps/index.ts","src/presentation-kit/Stage.tsx","src/presentation-kit/Presentation.tsx","src/presentation-kit/types.ts"],"marker":""},{"id":"demo-stable-identity-and-grouping","classification":"confirmed","rationale":"All nine steps come from one OUTLINE.map in steps/index.ts. Each gets the same Scene and the same groupKey, and only payload.stage differs. Stage keys the AnimatePresence child by sceneKey(step), which for a shared groupKey and Scene is a single `group:` key, so the scene stays mounted inside one LayoutGroup. The presentation folder keeps each responsibility in its own file. outline.ts holds TITLE and the narration. entities.ts holds the ID namespace, entity data and geometry. steps/Scene.tsx turns entities into kit nodes. steps/index.ts builds the Step list with one groupKey. Talk.tsx is a thin layer that wires Presentation, TITLE, STEPS and talk.css. presentations/index.ts is a registry with one entry that lazy-loads Talk. The public title contract is used, not ignored. Talk passes title={TITLE}, and Presentation destructures `title` and renders it as data-presentation-title-text on the root element. Every ID member reaches a rendered element. Scene.tsx sets `layoutId: e.id` on boxes, labels, chips and frames, and uses `key={e.id}` on each Appear wrapper, which covers the arrows. Judge A failed the criterion because it said CANVAS (entities.ts:108) has no consumer. That is wrong. A only searched the presentation-local runtime files. CANVAS is imported by tests/unit/sample/scene.test.tsx (lines 5-12), which is part of the delivered source. That test uses it to bound every entity rect and arrow point and asserts its value (lines 226-243), so it is a used geometry contract, not a dead one. It is not misleading either: its 880 x 380 matches the kit&#39;s DESIGN_W/DESIGN_H (constants.ts:4-5), which the default Stage design uses (Stage.tsx:8). A&#39;s stated reason therefore does not decide the requirement. Three test files drive a real browser, and none of them contains a fixed sleep or an immediate read used as a wait. These are tests/e2e/verify.test.ts, tests/integration/inspect.test.ts and tests/integration/bootstrap.test.ts, all quoted in full. Each one runs the verify or inspect script through run() and awaits the child&#39;s &#39;close&#39; event before asserting on the exit code, output or written PNGs (tests/helpers/project.ts:15-32). The timer in run() only bounds a hung child; it is not a wait for a transition. Inside the browser, every step change waits on observable state. inspect-presentation.mjs waits with waitForSelector(&#39;[data-step-count]&#39;) and then, after each ArrowRight, with waitForFunction on data-step-index === i, which has a timeout. render.mjs waitForIndex polls readState until the index equals the expected value; its 50 ms waitForTimeout is only the gap between polls. The only waitForTimeout in tests/unit/scripts/verify-core.test.ts belongs to a fakePage mock with no real browser. The setTimeout strings in verify.test.ts (lines 123, 135, 147) are fault code injected into the fixture scene, not test waits. Judges A and B said pass, and the material bears out their reasons. Judge C said fail because inspect.test.ts passes --settle=300 and the settling test compares captures taken with fixed settles of 0, 1200 and 2500 ms. That reason does not decide the requirement. The settle delay at inspect-presentation.mjs:67 runs only after the polling waitForFunction at line 65 has confirmed the step index, so it never replaces the state wait. The settling test is a test of the settle parameter itself: it asserts on output files after the process exits, not on step state after a sleep. The guidance also says longer fixed settle delays are validator noise that no engineering criterion scores. It does show state waits: inspect-presentation.mjs:65 waits with waitForFunction on data-step-index, and render.mjs:33-44 polls the index. The ruling argues that the settle runs after the index wait, and that &#39;longer fixed settle delays&#39; is validator noise. Neither point saves the pass. The noise clause only says no credit is given for, and nothing fails for the absence of, longer settle delays. It does not exempt existing fixed sleeps from the &#39;no fixed sleeps&#39; clause. The guidance also fails any test that &#39;waits a fixed number of milliseconds … for a transition before asserting&#39;. The motion requirement (the candidate&#39;s ledger restates it as &#39;departing entities to animate out&#39;, and SKILL.md says departing ones &#39;fade out&#39;) has a user-visible exit outcome that no recorded observation shows. The round-0 floor marks departures &#39;exercised&#39; through E-4. E-4 only counts entity wrappers after a 3 s settle, so it shows that departed entities are absent, not that they animate out. This is the kind of weaker-property check (DOM state instead of motion) that the criterion says does not cover a scenario.
